Andy Ogles addresses amnesty opposition, Senate leadership criticism, and OpenAI cyber incident
Rep. Andy Ogles, U.S. Congressman representing Tennessee's 5th district and Chairman of the Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection, made a series of statements on July 22, 2026, via his official Twitter account addressing immigration policy, Senate leadership, and cybersecurity concerns.
In a post at 19:10 UTC, Ogles stated his opposition to amnesty proposals in Congress: "I will fight AGAINST any amnesty proposal in Congress. Illegal aliens BROKE our laws, and they MUST go home. AMNESTY is betraying the trust of the American people."
Later that evening at 20:35 UTC, he commented on Senate leadership regarding election security legislation: "If John Thune has shown that he does not want to put the SAVE America Act on the Senate floor, he should step aside. There are plenty of other options in the Senate capable of securing our elections as Majority Leader. @BasedMikeLee @SenRickScott Interested?"
At 22:00 UTC on July 22, Ogles addressed recent developments involving artificial intelligence and cybersecurity: "OpenAI’s reported autonomous AI cyber incident should be a wake-up call. As Chairman of the Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection, I'm calling for better coordination between Congress, my Subcommittee, federal agencies, and the companies."
The SAVE America Act referenced by Ogles is part of ongoing legislative efforts aimed at strengthening election security measures within the United States Senate.
As chairman of a key House subcommittee focused on cybersecurity and infrastructure protection, Ogles' comments follow increasing concern about potential vulnerabilities in both government systems and private sector technology platforms.
